questions.q: What does community detection identify in a graph?
options: The single most important node in the entire graph
Groups of nodes that are more densely connected to each other than to the rest of the graph
The shortest path between any two nodes
Which nodes have no relationships at all
questions.explain: Community detection finds clusters of densely interconnected nodes, distinct from centrality (which node matters most) or pathfinding (how to get between nodes).

questions.q: What metric does the Louvain algorithm optimize?
options: The total number of relationships in the graph
The shortest weighted path between all node pairs
Modularity — how much more densely connected nodes within a proposed community are compared to random chance
Degree centrality of every node
questions.explain: Louvain iteratively merges nodes into communities whenever doing so improves modularity, a measure of community density versus randomness.

questions.q: How does Louvain decide how many communities to find?
options: The user must specify an exact number of communities before running it
It always produces exactly one community per node label
It requires a separate machine learning model to determine community count first
It discovers both the number of communities and their membership automatically from the graph's structure, with no need to specify a count in advance
questions.explain: Louvain builds communities iteratively based on modularity improvement, discovering the natural grouping rather than requiring a predefined count.

questions.q: What is the key tradeoff of using Label Propagation instead of Louvain?
options: Label Propagation always produces higher-quality communities than Louvain
There is no real difference between the two algorithms
Label Propagation cannot be run on graphs with more than 10 nodes
Label Propagation is significantly faster on large graphs but can produce slightly different community boundaries between runs due to some randomness in propagation order
questions.explain: Label Propagation trades some consistency for significantly better speed on very large graphs.

questions.q: Which of these is named in the lesson as a real use case for community detection?
options: Computing the shortest path for GPS routing
Encrypting a database connection at rest
Detecting fraud rings — accounts that transact heavily with each other but rarely with the rest of the network
Enforcing a primary key constraint
questions.explain: The lesson names fraud ring detection, social network clustering, and product grouping as real community detection use cases.
